definitions.meaning: The turn between two arms that meet at a point called the vertex, measured in degrees.
An angle of exactly 90 degrees; smaller than that is acute, and bigger is obtuse.
The measuring tool for angles: put its centre dot on the vertex and its baseline along one arm, then read the scale.
The corner point where the two arms of an angle meet.

mechanismSteps: Right, acute, obtuse — spot the size: a right angle is exactly 90 degrees, smaller than that is acute, and bigger is obtuse.
Measuring with a protractor: line the centre dot up with the vertex and the baseline with one arm, then read where the other arm crosses the scale.
Angles on a straight line, angles at a point: angles sharing a straight line add to 180 degrees, and a full spin around one point is 360 degrees.
Triangle angle sum, quadrilateral corners: the three corners of a triangle add to 180 degrees, and the four corners of a quadrilateral add to 360 degrees.
Misconception: longer arms, same angle: the long arms look bigger, but the angle only measures the turn between the arms.
objectives: Name an angle as acute, right or obtuse from its size in degrees
Measure angles with a protractor and add angles on a straight line, at a point, and in a triangle
subject: math
title: Angles: identify, measure, add

trap.explanation: Longer arms look more impressive, and size is judged by the drawing rather than the turn. An angle measures the turn between the arms: same turn, same angle, whatever the arm lengths. In the animation scene s5 the same 45-degree angle is drawn twice, once with longer arms, and the turn between the arms never changes.
trap.misconception: The angle with longer arms is bigger.

workedExample: In scene s3, two angles sit on a straight line and one is 65 degrees. Angles on a straight line add to 180 degrees, so the missing angle is 180 - 65 = 115 degrees. Check: 115 + 65 = 180, so the line is complete and 115 degrees is correct.
